title: Remote Control (Tablet and Phone)
text:
With **remote control** you operate OpenCue from an iPad, tablet, phone or any other computer in the **same network** – while the console computer keeps running the show and sending the DMX. Walk through the room and adjust lights, trigger cues from the stage, or use a tablet as a second screen.

Remote control is **off by default**. As long as it is off, OpenCue is not reachable from the network at all (the port is really closed, not just password-protected).

title: 1. The idea in one minute
text:
- The **console** is the computer where OpenCue is installed and running. It does all the work: it holds the show, calculates the cues and sends DMX.
- A **remote device** is just a browser. It opens a web address of the console, logs in with the password and shows **the same OpenCue interface** – same toolbar, same panels, same rights.
- Everything stays in sync live: when you select a fixture, move a fader or press *Go* on one device, all others show it immediately.
- No internet is needed. Everything happens inside your local network.

title: 2. Switching it on
text:
1. On the console open **Settings** (toolbar) → category **Remote**.
2. Turn on the **Remote access master switch** at the top. **There is no default password:** the first time OpenCue asks for your own - **"Choose a password"**, entered twice (at least 4 characters; *Cancel* switches remote access off again). **HTTP** is on afterwards.
3. The **password** is set and changed under **Settings → Security** (button *Set or change password ...* in the Remote section); this also works from a remote device (its own login is carried along; all other devices have to log in again). Use *Show* to check what you typed. The same password protects the lock screen (section 8).  Any password is allowed (at least 4 characters) - the choice is yours.
4. Optionally change the **HTTP port** (1024–65535, default 8000). A changed port takes effect after restarting OpenCue.
   **HTTPS** is its own section below with its own switch and its own **HTTPS port** (default 8001, takes effect at once): some browser features need a **secure page (https)**: **keeping the iPad screen awake** (Settings → More options → *Keep the screen awake*), the VR mode of the 3D simulation, and microphone and camera in the browser. So open the **https:// address** on the iPad (confirm the certificate once); over `http://` only the device setting "Auto-lock: Never" works. OpenCue creates the certificate itself; the browser asks once to confirm it on the first visit. HTTP and HTTPS can be switched on and off independently and each has its own address with its own QR code.
   **Network name:** the console is also reachable as `opencue.local` (it comes automatically with remote access; a small switch under *Advanced*), for example `http://opencue.local:8000` - the address stays the same in every network. If the name is already taken (for example by a second console), OpenCue uses `opencue-2.local` and so on; the settings show which one applies. iPad, iPhone, Mac and Windows 10/11 understand the name on their own. An installed web app is bound to its address: if you switch to the name, install it once more.
5. Click **Save** (the dialog stays open). No restart is needed. The first time, Windows asks about the firewall once - allow **private networks**.

title: 2. Switching it on (2)
text:
OpenCue now listens on every network address of the console. The page shows:

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Status** | “Reachable on the network” or “Local only”. |
| **Addresses** | Every address under which the console can be reached, each with a **Copy** button. |
| **QR code** | For the selected address – scan it with the camera of an iPad or phone. The password is asked when connecting. |
| **Detect addresses again** | After you changed Wi-Fi or plugged in a cable. |

When you switch it off again, the listeners are closed again, immediately.

> **Windows firewall:** when remote access is switched on for the first time, Windows may ask whether OpenCue may communicate on the network. Allow it for your **private** network; otherwise other devices cannot connect.

title: 3. Connecting a device
text:
1. Make sure the device is in the **same network** (same Wi-Fi or LAN) as the console.
2. Open the address from the settings page in the device's browser – for example `http://192.168.1.20:8000/` – or scan the QR code. The address redirects to the remote page `/remote/`.
3. Enter the password and tap **Sign in**.

**Save password** (checkbox on the login page) stores the password in the browser of **that device only** and pre-fills the field next time. There is no automatic login – you still tap *Sign in*. Untick the box to delete the stored password immediately.

**Wrong password:** repeated wrong attempts lock the device out for a while (brute-force protection).

**Sign out:** *File → Sign out* (only shown on remote devices).

If nothing connects: check that both devices are in the same network (guest Wi-Fi networks often separate devices from each other), that the address matches the one on the settings page, and the firewall (see above).

path: 4. What a remote device can do
title: 4. What a remote device can do
text:
- **Everything the console can do.** After logging in, a remote device has the same rights: programming, cues, effects, files, settings, DMX settings and remote settings. That includes things with consequences – switching off remote access (which locks that device out) or **quitting OpenCue**, which stops the program for everybody. Use a password that only people you trust know.
- **Own layout per device.** Each device remembers which layout it used and can show a different one than the console. Build a layout for the tablet with big buttons (see below). If one device saves a layout that another device currently shows, the other one takes it over – or, if it has unsaved changes of its own, offers *Apply* or *Keep my version*.
- **Full access to all settings, also from the iPad.** This matters when OpenCue runs without a window (*server only*, tray icon): all settings - output, security and lock mode, REST API, AI assistant, voice control, backups, start with Windows, defaults, inputs / outputs ... - can be changed on the iPad and apply **to the server**. The microphone switch of voice control is there on the iPad as well. **Folders:** where the main computer would open the Windows Explorer, a remote device gets the **OpenCue Explorer** - a large dialog for the OpenCue data folder (shows, backups, logs, fixtures ...): browse, download (a folder as ZIP), upload, new folder, rename, duplicate, delete. It cannot leave the data folder. The same dialog (*Choose folder...*) lets you pick a new storage location. **MIDI learning / monitoring**, the **DMX input** and the **firewall rule** (Windows asks for permission on the main computer) also work from the iPad. Only a few things hang **physically on the main computer**: its window (fullscreen), the **lock screen** of the console (unlock it there), recording the key of a **specific keyboard**, the **microphone while dictating** and the real Windows Explorer.
- **Per device:** only the **fullscreen mode** (each browser's own) and the **GUI scale**.
- **Data stays on the console.** Saving and loading always go through the console; shows, layouts and fixtures live on the console computer.

path: 4. What a remote device can do
title: Who is connected?
text: A toolbar icon shows **how many remote devices are connected**. Click it to see IP address, device and connection time of each – and to **disconnect** (*Kick*) a device. A disconnected device sees a notice and must reload the page to log in again.

path: 5. Install as an app (iPad / iPhone / Android)
title: 5. Install as an app (iPad / iPhone / Android)
text:
The remote page is a **web app**. On the device you can add it to the home screen:

- **iPad / iPhone (Safari):** Share button → **Add to Home Screen**.
- **Android (Chrome):** menu → **Install app** / **Add to Home screen**.

It then opens full-screen without browser bars, with the colours of your current theme.

**Icon:** the app gets the OpenCue icon and the name "OpenCue" – also over HTTPS. (The icon is embedded in the page; otherwise iOS does not fetch it from a self-made certificate and shows only a grey letter.) If the icon still does not change, delete the app from the home screen and add it again – iOS remembers the old icon.

path: 5. Install as an app (iPad / iPhone / Android)
title: 5. Install as an app (iPad / iPhone / Android) (2)
text: **Offline page and server choice (secure page, HTTPS):** when the server cannot be reached, the app shows "**Server not reachable**" instead of an error page. There you can **Reload**, or enter a new **address or IP**, the **port** and **HTTPS** on / off under **Other server** and **Connect** – if the computer has a new IP address you do not have to reinstall the app. The recently used addresses are listed below to tap. If the connection drops (Wi-Fi gone, OpenCue closed), the notice "Restoring the connection" appears; after 3 seconds with the button "**Choose another server (7s)**" whose number **counts down**; at 0 the offline page opens by itself and loads OpenCue again as soon as the server answers. This also applies when Wi-Fi is there but the computer does not answer – then the offline page appears after **about 1.5 seconds** instead of a white screen and disappears again immediately when the server does answer. If you open it on purpose with the button, it stays. Tip: the name `opencue.local` finds the computer even when the IP changes.

path: 5. Install as an app (iPad / iPhone / Android)
title: 5. Install as an app (iPad / iPhone / Android) (3)
text: **Important on the iPad – install the certificate once:** with a self-made certificate iOS only knows the exception "continue despite the warning" **inside the Safari tab**. An app from the Home Screen then stays **white**, and the service worker (offline page) is not allowed. So OpenCue creates its own certificate authority ("OpenCue Local CA") that signs the https certificate. You install it **once** on the device:

path: 5. Install as an app (iPad / iPhone / Android)
title: 5. Install as an app (iPad / iPhone / Android) (4)
text: The steps are a **guide page** on the server: *Settings → Remote access → Certificate for iPad and browsers* shows its address and a QR code (scan it with the iPad camera). The page opens over **http://** without a login and follows the device language. At the top you choose between **iPad / iPhone** and **Android · Windows · macOS**. For the iPad there are four steps with a reminder: **Download → Install → Trust → Open https**; you can tick off finished steps (the page remembers them). **Important: open the page in Safari** – the profile cannot be installed from the home-screen app, from Chrome or from the browser inside another app. "Settings" means the **Settings app of the iPad**, not a setting in Safari. At the end of each page it says how to **remove the certificate again** (iPad: Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → "OpenCue" → Remove Profile). In OpenCue the same is under *Settings → Remote access → Certificate for iPad and browsers* (short version for installing and removing). (Access over HTTP must be on for this.)

path: 5. Install as an app (iPad / iPhone / Android)
title: 5. Install as an app (iPad / iPhone / Android) (5)
text:
From then on https works without a warning, the app opens, the service worker and the offline page run – also when the computer gets a **new IP address** (OpenCue only re-issues the server certificate, the authority stays). The authority may only vouch for local names (`.local`, `localhost`) and private addresses. Android / Windows / macOS: install the certificate file (`opencue-ca.crt`) and set it up as a trusted authority. If you delete the `https` folder in the data folder, a new authority is created – install the profile on the devices again.

**Limitation:** installable web apps and the offline page need a secure connection (HTTPS, on the iPad with the installed certificate). Over plain `http://` the home-screen app works, but there is no offline page and the device must reach the console to show anything.

path: 6. Tips for a good tablet layout
title: 6. Tips for a good tablet layout
text:
- Create a **separate layout** for the tablet (*Edit → Manage Layouts…*): large **Executor**, **Cue List**, a few **Button** or **Fader** panels and the **Fixture Control** category you need most. Remote devices load their own layout, so the console layout stays as it is.
- For touch use the panels **Command Numpad** and **Command Buttons** instead of typing on the screen keyboard.
- Increase the **GUI scale** on the tablet (`Ctrl +` or *View → GUI Scale…*) – it applies to that device only.
- Layouts can be switched by **swiping** horizontally if *Settings → General → Switch layouts by swiping* is on (per device).
- Cue lists with timecode triggers keep running on the console even if a device disconnects – the show does not depend on the tablet.

title: 7. Safety and good practice
text:
- Use remote control only in networks you trust (your own router, a dedicated show network). The connection is **not encrypted** (plain HTTP); anyone in the network could read the traffic.
- Choose a password you do not use elsewhere – it is stored in the app configuration on the console and, if you tick *Save password*, in the browser of that device.
- Switch remote off when you do not need it.
- DMX output always runs on the console – even if all remote devices disconnect, the lights stay as they are.

path: 8. Lock: lock screen and logging out
title: 8. Lock: lock screen and logging out
text:
**Settings → Security** has the **lock mode** (off by default, needs the password):

- **At the console:** the **padlock** in the top bar, **Ctrl+L** (changeable under *Controls → Keyboard shortcuts*) or **Controls → Lock** locks OpenCue. A locked console shows only a dark password window - the rest of the interface is hidden, the keyboard does nothing, and the console no longer accepts changes from this window (not even past the interface). A reload does **not** unlock. **The show keeps running:** cues, effects, MIDI, OSC, the schedule and remote devices work as before. Five wrong passwords in a row pause the unlocking for a minute. The password never leaves the console while it is locked. Restarting OpenCue unlocks.
- **At a remote device:** the padlock **logs the device out**: the session ends, the *Save password* of that device is erased, and the page shows the login again with an empty password field. Remote devices cannot change the password or the lock mode.
- **Lock automatically after ...** (1 to 60 minutes without any input; off by default): the console locks itself, remote devices log out. Be careful with a tablet that only displays: leave the setting off for those.

path: 9. Simple control and operator mode (to hand the console to someone else)
title: 9. Simple control and operator mode (to hand the console to someone else)
text:
- **Panel "Simple control"** (*Edit → Add Panel → Input*) is the plain sister of the *Fixture Control* panel and uses the **whole panel** with fixed, percentage-based fields: on the left (38 %) **every fixture has its own tile** (number, name, live colour and brightness), sorted by **groups** (tap the group name = select the whole group; the rest sorted by type; *All* / *None* at the top); on the right **brightness** (big fader, *Off* / *Full*), **colour** (colour field - hue left to right, more white towards the top - plus colour buttons), **move** (spring **joystick**: push - the further, the faster; let go = stop; *Centre*), **zoom**, **gobos** as pictures, a big **Blackout** button and the **looks**: *Rainbow*, *Circle* (pan / tilt), *Pulse*, *Strobe* - ready-made standard effects without any setting (tap again = off, *Looks off* removes all; the effect is added to the show automatically the first time). A control that the selected lights do not have stays in its place but is dimmed. On a **narrow panel** (under about 720 px) it switches to a **compact mode** with one tab per area (*Lights | Brightness | Colour | Move | Beam | Looks*; Blackout stays visible). Nothing here changes groups or the show; selection, values and effects are the ones of the whole program (programmer, cues, effect studio). Make a layout with only this panel (or a few more) for the person who should operate.
- **Operator mode** (*View → Operator mode ...* or the joystick button in the top bar; needs the password, *Settings → Security*): this device can **only operate** what is on the screen - no menus, no top bar, no settings or other dialogs, no keyboard shortcuts (typing in a text field still works), no moving or rebuilding panels, no switching of layout or show. You leave it with the small **padlock at the bottom right** and the password, or with **Ctrl+L**. It is started only from the menu or the button (no keyboard shortcut). **Commands** (command line, keys, widgets) are executed by the server in operator mode only if they **operate**; whatever changes the show (*Store, Update, Delete, Move, Label, Set*, cue times, creating / renaming / deleting cue lists) is refused - also inside a command chain. **At the console voice control is off in operator mode** (the microphone stays closed) and comes back afterwards if it is switched on. The **server enforces it**: from a device in operator mode only operating messages are accepted (select, set values, cues, presets, timecode, command line ...); programming, layout, show and settings messages are dropped and write requests are answered with `423`. A reload does not leave the mode. It works at the console and at every remote device on its own (hand over an iPad with the app in operator mode); restarting OpenCue ends it. Five wrong passwords in a row pause the exit for a minute.
- **Good to know:** the command line, if you put it into that layout, can run any command - leave it out of a layout for guests. Keys of a dedicated extra keyboard (*Custom keyboard shortcuts*, device-specific) and MIDI / OSC controllers keep working: they belong to the show, not to the screen.
